title: Error Prevention
verify: Every irreversible or bulk action (delete, purge, bulk write, payment) shows a confirmation step naming what will be affected, and its trigger sits apart from the safe primary action.
anti_pattern: A red Delete button placed right next to Save that removes the record on a single click with no confirmation and no undo.

title: Inline Validation — Validate on Field Blur, Not on Keystroke
verify: Typing a partial valid value (e.g. the first characters of an email) in a standard field shows no error until the field loses focus or the form is submitted.
anti_pattern: An onChange handler that sets the error state, so "Invalid email" appears after the first typed character.

title: Postel's Law — Accept Varied Input, Output Consistent Data
verify: Entering the same phone number as "555-123-4567", "(555) 123 4567" and " 5551234567 " is accepted in all three cases and stored in one normalized format.
anti_pattern: A strict regex like /^\d{10}$/ that rejects dashes, spaces or surrounding whitespace with "Invalid format".

title: Keep Forms as Short as Possible — Eliminate Unnecessary Fields
verify: Every field in the form is either needed to complete the current task or clearly marked optional, and none asks for data already available from the account.
anti_pattern: A signup form that asks for company size, phone, job title and address before the user can create an account, and re-asks the email in a second field.

title: Single-Column Form Layouts and Logical Field Sequencing
verify: In a form with more than 3 fields, each row holds one field, except short inseparable groups (First/Last name, City/State/ZIP), and the tab order matches the visual order.
anti_pattern: A two-column grid of unrelated fields (Email next to Company, Password next to Role) that makes the eye zig-zag.

title: Group Related Form Fields With Section Headings
verify: A form with more than ~6 fields splits them into sections with a visible heading each, with more space between sections than between fields inside one.
anti_pattern: A 15-field form as one flat list with uniform spacing, no headings, and Save and Delete in the same block.

title: Never Use Placeholder Text as a Substitute for Labels
verify: Every input has a persistent visible label (a <label> bound to it) that stays on screen after the user types, and the placeholder never carries the only description of the field.
anti_pattern: <input placeholder="Email"> with no <label>, so the field name disappears once the user starts typing (jsx-a11y/label-has-associated-control catches the missing label).

title: Smart Defaults in Forms and Configuration
verify: On a new record form, fields that can be inferred (owner = current user, date range = last full period, country/timezone/currency from the account) arrive pre-filled.
anti_pattern: "Assigned to" left blank, date range defaulting to "All time", and timezone showing "Select..." even though the account already has one.

title: Appropriate Control Selection for Form Inputs
verify: Mutually exclusive choices of 2-5 options use radios, independent multi-selects use checkboxes, and structured data (date, number) does not use a plain text input.
anti_pattern: Checkboxes for mutually exclusive options (allowing impossible states) or a free-text input for a date that accepts "tomorrow-ish".

title: Enterprise Form Design
verify: Each field has its label above the input, shows its error/success state after blur, and a long form keeps Save/Cancel visible without scrolling.
anti_pattern: Validation that only runs on submit, labels living inside the input as placeholders, and Save buttons at the bottom of a 3-screen-tall form.

title: Match Input Field Type and Size to Expected Input
verify: Field width reflects expected length (a ZIP field is visibly short, a description is a multi-line textarea) and numeric fields use type=number or inputmode with min/max.
anti_pattern: A full-width single-line input for a 5-digit ZIP code, and a one-line text input for a multi-paragraph comment.

title: Progress Communication in Multi-Step Forms
verify: A multi-step form shows the full list of steps with the current one highlighted from step 1, and states before starting what documents are needed and whether progress can be saved.
anti_pattern: A wizard that reveals one step at a time with no step count, so the user learns on step 4 that a tax ID document is required.

title: Prioritized Multi-Error Display
verify: A field that fails several rules shows exactly one error message at a time, the format error before range or cross-field errors.
anti_pattern: Entering "abc" in a numeric field shows "Must be a number", "Must be between 1 and 100" and "Must be less than End" at the same time.

title: Save & Resume for Long Forms
verify: Reloading or reopening a form mid-way restores the last step with all previously entered values, and a "Last saved" timestamp is visible near the primary action.
anti_pattern: State kept only in component memory, so a tab refresh or session timeout after 10 minutes of typing returns an empty step 1.
